Riyadh EV Auto Show · What I experienced and the questions I took away.

  • My 2025 annual reflection mentions experiencing electric buses at the Riyadh EV Auto Show. The annual reflection places this alongside aviation events and cybersecurity learning as an example of exploring how technology is reshaping different industries.
  • Transport connects several of my interests. Aviation first made me think about operations and coordination. Electric mobility adds a different question: how does a product change the experience of getting from one place to another? I am interested in the technology, but also in the people it is intended to serve.
  • My later interest in CEER brought me back to practical design and the local setting around a product. I like asking how an innovation addresses an actual need, instead of simply noticing that it is new. The intended user's experience is a useful place to begin that question.
  • The visit was one small part of a year spent exploring different industries in Riyadh. I wanted to keep the electric-bus experience alongside the other things that caught my attention. Together, they show why I became more interested in the organisations around a product and the people who depend on it.

The experience preserved in my annual reflection

My 2025 annual reflection mentions experiencing electric buses at the Riyadh EV Auto Show.

The annual reflection places this alongside aviation events and cybersecurity learning as an example of exploring how technology is reshaping different industries.

The connection

I mentioned the visit in my annual reflection, alongside aviation events and cybersecurity learning.

Read the deeper context+

The electric buses were the part I chose to remember. It was a brief experience, but it added another angle to my interest in transport and in how technology changes the way people use a service.

02 / 04

Mobility as a wider interest

Transport connects several of my interests.

Aviation first made me think about operations and coordination. Electric mobility adds a different question: how does a product change the experience of getting from one place to another? I am interested in the technology, but also in the people it is intended to serve.

The connection

I want to understand the organisation around a mobility product as well as the product itself.

Read the deeper context+

Who is it intended to serve? Which conditions need to be in place for it to be useful? What evidence would show that the proposed benefits are being realised? Those are questions for further study.

03 / 04

From product interest to commercial questions

My later interest in CEER brought me back to practical design and the local setting around a product.

I like asking how an innovation addresses an actual need, instead of simply noticing that it is new. The intended user's experience is a useful place to begin that question.

The connection

My interest in corporate law makes the commercial side of mobility more engaging too.

Read the deeper context+

A product sits within an organisation and a market, with decisions about who it serves and what makes it useful. My business courses give me a starting point for asking about that wider setting and the purpose behind a launch.

04 / 04

A question to carry forward

The visit was one small part of a year spent exploring different industries in Riyadh.

I wanted to keep the electric-bus experience alongside the other things that caught my attention. Together, they show why I became more interested in the organisations around a product and the people who depend on it.

The connection

I would like to learn more about the business questions around mobility: what makes a service useful, how a company understands its users, and which conditions help a new product fit everyday life.

Read the deeper context+

Those questions connect the visit to my wider learning, while leaving plenty for me to investigate next.
